narrative:
The model estimates a 58% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key aspects of your profile.

Your relatively short overall work experience of 1-5 years was the strongest factor pushing the model toward predicting you would stay. Most employees the model expects to remain also fall into this early-career group, so the system sees this as a stabilizing influence. However, two other factors pulled more strongly in the opposite direction.

The fact that you have received other job offers while working here was the most important reason the model leaned toward you leaving. Having external opportunities clearly signals higher risk of departure compared with the majority of employees who stay and report receiving no such offers.

Your limited time in your current role (also 1-5 years) added a smaller but still noticeable push toward leaving. While many people the model expects to stay are also relatively new to their organization, your combination of short tenure here plus outside options outweighed the stabilizing effect of your overall experience.

The organization should discuss your career goals with you openly and explore whether additional responsibilities, clearer growth paths, or retention measures could reduce the appeal of outside opportunities. You may also wish to reflect on what would make you want to build a longer-term future here.
